subject: bnss
question: The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, which replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, came into force on:
explanation: The BNSS came into force on 1 July 2024 by Central Government notification under Section 1(3), together with the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam. Section 531 repeals the CrPC, 1973, while saving appeals, applications, trials, inquiries and investigations pending on that date, which continue under the old Code.

subject: bnss
question: Information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence (the First Information Report) is recorded by the officer in charge of a police station under which section of the BNSS?
explanation: Section 173 of the BNSS governs information in cognizable cases and corresponds to Section 154 of the CrPC. Section 175 (old Section 156) deals with the power to investigate, Section 180 (old Section 161) with examination of witnesses, and Section 193 (old Section 173) with the final police report.

subject: bnss
question: The power of a police officer making an investigation to examine orally any person supposed to be acquainted with the facts of the case is found in:
explanation: Section 180 of the BNSS (old Section 161 CrPC) allows the investigating officer to examine orally any person supposed to be acquainted with the facts and circumstances of the case and to reduce the statement to writing. Section 181 (old Section 162) restricts the use of such statements, and Section 179 (old Section 160) deals with requiring the attendance of witnesses.

subject: bnss
question: Under Section 58 of the BNSS, a police officer shall not detain in custody a person arrested without warrant for longer than ______, exclusive of the time necessary for the journey to the Magistrate's court, without a Magistrate's order.
explanation: Section 58 of the BNSS (old Section 57 CrPC) bars detention of a person arrested without warrant beyond twenty-four hours, exclusive of journey time to the Magistrate's court, in the absence of a special order under Section 187. It gives effect to the guarantee in Article 22(2) of the Constitution.

subject: bnss
question: An order for maintenance of wives, children and parents is made by a Magistrate under:
explanation: Section 144 of the BNSS provides for orders of maintenance of wives, children and parents and corresponds to Section 125 of the CrPC. Section 163 of the BNSS (old Section 144 CrPC) deals with urgent cases of nuisance or apprehended danger, so the old and new numbers must not be confused.

subject: bnss
question: A direction for the grant of bail to a person apprehending arrest for a non-bailable offence (anticipatory bail) is given under:
explanation: Section 482 of the BNSS empowers the High Court or Court of Session to grant anticipatory bail and corresponds to Section 438 of the CrPC. Section 478 (old 436) covers bail in bailable offences, Section 480 (old 437) bail in non-bailable offences, and Section 483 (old 439) the special powers of the High Court and Court of Session regarding bail.

subject: bnss
question: The saving of the inherent powers of the High Court to make orders necessary to give effect to any order under the Sanhita, prevent abuse of the process of any court or otherwise secure the ends of justice is in:
explanation: Section 528 of the BNSS saves the inherent powers of the High Court and corresponds to Section 482 of the CrPC. Section 482 of the BNSS now deals with anticipatory bail, Section 530 with trials and proceedings in electronic mode, and Section 531 with repeal and savings.

subject: bnss
question: Bail as of right for a person accused of a bailable offence is provided in:
explanation: Section 478 of the BNSS (old Section 436 CrPC) provides that a person accused of a bailable offence who is arrested or detained without warrant and is prepared to give bail shall be released on bail. Section 479 (old 436A) deals with the maximum period of detention of undertrial prisoners.

subject: bnss
question: Confessions and statements are recorded by a Judicial Magistrate in the course of an investigation under:
explanation: Section 183 of the BNSS (old Section 164 CrPC) empowers a Judicial Magistrate to record confessions and statements during investigation, after warning the person that he is not bound to confess and that the confession may be used against him. The BNSS allows the confession or statement to be recorded by audio-video electronic means in the presence of the accused's advocate.

subject: bnss
question: Under Section 173(1) of the BNSS, information about a cognizable offence may be given to the officer in charge of a police station:
options: only if the offence was committed within the limits of that police station
irrespective of the area where the offence was committed
only after a Magistrate's permission when the offence occurred elsewhere
only in writing and in person
explanation: Section 173(1) of the BNSS allows information relating to a cognizable offence to be given irrespective of the area where the offence is committed, giving statutory form to the "zero FIR". The old Section 154 CrPC contained no such words, though courts had recognised the practice; the FIR is then transferred to the police station having jurisdiction.

subject: bnss
question: Where information about a cognizable offence is given by electronic communication under Section 173(1)(ii) of the BNSS, it shall be taken on record on being signed by the informant within:
explanation: Section 173(1)(ii) of the BNSS provides that information given by electronic communication shall be taken on record by the officer on being signed within three days by the person giving it. The provision on e-FIRs is new; the old Section 154 CrPC dealt only with oral and written information.

subject: bnss
question: Under Section 173(3) of the BNSS, for a cognizable offence punishable with imprisonment of three years or more but less than seven years, the officer in charge may, with the prior permission of an officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police, conduct a preliminary enquiry to ascertain whether a prima facie case exists within:
explanation: Section 173(3) of the BNSS permits, for offences punishable with three years or more but less than seven years, either a preliminary enquiry within fourteen days to ascertain a prima facie case, or immediate investigation, with the prior permission of a DSP-rank officer. Section 154 of the CrPC contained no statutory provision for a preliminary enquiry.

subject: bnss
question: Under Section 176(3) of the BNSS, for every offence punishable with imprisonment of seven years or more, the officer in charge of the police station shall, from a date notified by the State Government, cause:
options: the accused to be produced before the Sessions Judge
a forensic expert to visit the crime scene to collect forensic evidence and the process to be videographed
the case to be transferred to the CID
a Judicial Magistrate to supervise the investigation
explanation: Section 176(3) of the BNSS makes a forensic expert's visit to the crime scene and videography of the process mandatory for offences punishable with seven years or more, from a date the State Government notifies within five years. Section 176 otherwise corresponds to Section 157 of the CrPC (procedure for investigation).

subject: bnss
question: Under Section 187(3) of the BNSS, the maximum total period for which a Magistrate may authorise detention of an accused during investigation, where the offence is punishable with death, imprisonment for life or imprisonment for ten years or more, is:
explanation: Section 187(3) of the BNSS (old Section 167(2) CrPC) limits detention during investigation to ninety days where the offence is punishable with death, life imprisonment or imprisonment of ten years or more, and sixty days for any other offence. On expiry, the accused is entitled to be released on bail if prepared to furnish it (default bail).

subject: bnss
question: A Magistrate empowered under Section 210 of the BNSS may order an investigation into a cognizable case under Section 175(3), after considering an application supported by:
options: a certificate from the Public Prosecutor
a report from the Superintendent of Police alone
explanation: Section 175(3) of the BNSS (old Section 156(3) CrPC) allows the Magistrate to order investigation after considering an application supported by an affidavit under Section 173(4), after such inquiry as he thinks necessary and after considering the submission of the police officer. Section 173(4) applies where the officer in charge has refused to record the information and the Superintendent of Police has not acted on it.

subject: bnss
question: Under the first proviso to Section 223(1) of the BNSS, a Magistrate shall not take cognizance of an offence on a complaint:
options: without examining at least two witnesses
without giving the accused an opportunity of being heard
without the sanction of the Sessions Judge
explanation: Section 223 of the BNSS (old Section 200 CrPC) requires the Magistrate to examine the complainant and witnesses on oath, and its first proviso adds that no cognizance shall be taken without giving the accused an opportunity of being heard. That pre-cognizance hearing is new; the CrPC did not require it.

subject: bnss
question: Under Section 218 of the BNSS, where the Government fails to decide a request for sanction to prosecute a public servant within the prescribed period, sanction is deemed to have been accorded. That period is:
explanation: Section 218 of the BNSS (old Section 197 CrPC) requires previous sanction to prosecute judges and public servants for acts done in discharge of official duty. Its new proviso requires the Government to decide within one hundred and twenty days of receiving the request, failing which sanction is deemed to have been accorded.

subject: bnss
question: Where arrest is not required under Section 35(1) of the BNSS, the police officer shall issue a notice directing the person against whom a reasonable complaint has been made to appear before him. This notice of appearance corresponds to which provision of the old CrPC?
explanation: Section 35(3) to (6) of the BNSS carry forward the notice of appearance under Section 41A of the CrPC. Where the person complies with the notice and continues to comply, he shall not be arrested unless, for reasons recorded, the officer is of the opinion that he ought to be arrested; Section 35 as a whole corresponds to Section 41 of the CrPC.

subject: bnss
question: The duty of a police officer arresting a person without warrant to communicate the full particulars of the offence or other grounds of arrest, and to inform a person not accused of a non-bailable offence of the right to bail, is in:
explanation: Section 47 of the BNSS (old Section 50 CrPC) requires the arresting officer to communicate forthwith the full particulars of the offence or other grounds of arrest, and to inform a person arrested for an offence other than a non-bailable offence that he is entitled to be released on bail. Section 48 (old Section 50A) requires information about the arrest to be given to a nominated person.

subject: bnss
question: An order by an Executive Magistrate in urgent cases of nuisance or apprehended danger under Section 163 of the BNSS shall not, unless extended by the State Government, remain in force for more than:
explanation: Section 163(4) of the BNSS (old Section 144(4) CrPC) limits such an order to two months from the making of it. Under the proviso, the State Government may, if it considers it necessary for preventing danger to human life, health or safety or a riot, extend it by notification for up to six months from the date the Magistrate's order would otherwise have expired.

subject: bnss
question: The compounding of offences, listing which offences may be compounded with or without the permission of the court, is governed by:
explanation: Section 359 of the BNSS (old Section 320 CrPC) sets out the offences under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita that may be compounded by the specified persons, some without and some only with the court's permission. A composition has the effect of an acquittal (Section 359(8)); Section 360 (old 321) deals with withdrawal from prosecution.

subject: bnss
question: Under the proviso to Section 413 of the BNSS, the victim has a right to prefer an appeal against an order of the court:
options: acquitting the accused, convicting for a lesser offence or imposing inadequate compensation
explanation: Section 413 of the BNSS (old Section 372 CrPC) provides that no appeal lies except as provided by the Sanhita or any other law. Its proviso gives the victim a right to appeal against an order acquitting the accused, convicting for a lesser offence or imposing inadequate compensation, to the court to which an appeal ordinarily lies against a conviction.

subject: bnss
question: Section 398 of the BNSS requires every State Government to:
options: establish a special court for witness intimidation
prepare and notify a Witness Protection Scheme for the State
pay travel allowance to all witnesses
record the evidence of all witnesses by video conferencing
explanation: Section 398 of the BNSS directs every State Government to prepare and notify a Witness Protection Scheme for the State with a view to ensuring the protection of witnesses. The CrPC had no corresponding provision.

subject: bnss
question: Under Section 105 of the BNSS, the process of conducting a search and seizure, including preparing the list of seized items and its signing by witnesses, shall be:
options: recorded through audio-video electronic means, preferably a mobile phone, and forwarded without delay to the Magistrate
conducted only in the presence of a Judicial Magistrate
recorded only in the case diary
conducted only between sunrise and sunset
explanation: Section 105 of the BNSS, which has no equivalent in the CrPC, requires search and seizure under Chapter VII or Section 185 to be recorded through audio-video electronic means, preferably a mobile phone. The police officer must forward the recording without delay to the District Magistrate, Sub-divisional Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the first class.

subject: bnss
question: Under the proviso to Section 479(1) of the BNSS, an undertrial prisoner who is a first-time offender (never convicted of any offence) shall be released on bond by the court if he has undergone detention for up to:
options: one-half of the maximum period of imprisonment for the offence
one-fourth of the maximum period of imprisonment for the offence
two-thirds of the maximum period of imprisonment for the offence
one-third of the maximum period of imprisonment for the offence
explanation: Section 479(1) of the BNSS (old Section 436A CrPC) entitles an undertrial, other than one accused of an offence punishable with death or life imprisonment, to release on bail after detention for one-half of the maximum term. Its new proviso reduces this to one-third for a first-time offender, and Section 479(2) bars such release where investigation, inquiry or trial is pending in more than one offence.

flags.note: New first-time-offender proviso in Section 479 BNSS; confirm wording.
The Supreme Court (In re Inhuman Conditions in 1382 Prisons, 2024) applied this proviso to undertrials whose cases began before 1 July 2024. Check whether it should be mentioned.

subject: bnss
question: Section 356 of the BNSS, which has no counterpart in the CrPC, permits:
options: the trial of a proclaimed offender who has absconded to evade trial, in his absence, as if he were present
the trial of a juvenile by a Court of Session
the summary trial of all offences punishable up to seven years
the transfer of a trial to a court outside India
explanation: Section 356 of the BNSS provides for inquiry, trial and judgment in absentia where a person declared a proclaimed offender has absconded to evade trial and there is no immediate prospect of arresting him; this is deemed a waiver of his right to be present. Safeguards include notices and the appointment of an advocate for his defence; the CrPC (Section 299) only allowed evidence to be recorded in the absence of the accused.

subject: bnss
question: Under Section 23 of the BNSS, a Judicial Magistrate of the first class may pass a sentence of imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years, or of fine not exceeding ______, or both, or of community service.
explanation: Section 23(2) of the BNSS (old Section 29(2) CrPC) raises the fine a Judicial Magistrate of the first class may impose from ten thousand to fifty thousand rupees, and adds community service as a sentence. A Judicial Magistrate of the second class may impose up to one year's imprisonment, a fine up to ten thousand rupees, or community service (Section 23(3)).

flags.note: Confirm the fine limits in Section 23(2) and (3) BNSS (Rs. 50,000 and Rs. 10,000) against the bare act.

subject: bnss
question: Under Section 187(2) and (3) of the BNSS, police custody of an accused during investigation may be authorised for a total not exceeding fifteen days, which:
options: must be taken only within the first fifteen days after arrest, as under the CrPC
may be taken in whole or in parts at any time during the initial forty or sixty days of the sixty- or ninety-day detention period
may be taken at any time until the charge-sheet is filed, without limit
may be extended to thirty days with the Sessions Judge's approval
explanation: Section 187 of the BNSS (old Section 167 CrPC) allows police custody of up to fifteen days in the whole or in parts at any time during the initial forty days or sixty days out of the sixty- or ninety-day detention period. Under the CrPC, as read in CBI v. Anupam J. Kulkarni (1992), police custody was confined to the first fifteen days after production.

flags.note: New split-custody rule in Section 187 BNSS; confirm wording.
Mentions CBI v. Anupam J. Kulkarni (1992). Courts are still interpreting the new provision.

subject: bnss
question: Under Section 35(7) of the BNSS, no arrest shall be made without the prior permission of an officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police where the offence is punishable with imprisonment for less than three years and the person is:
options: infirm or above sixty years of age
explanation: Section 35(7) of the BNSS is a new safeguard requiring the prior permission of a DSP-rank officer before arresting a person who is infirm or above sixty years of age for an offence punishable with less than three years' imprisonment. The rest of Section 35 carries forward Sections 41 and 41A of the CrPC on arrest without warrant and notice of appearance.

subject: bnss
question: Section 107 of the BNSS, which has no counterpart in the CrPC, empowers the Magistrate, on the application of a police officer, to:
options: order the attachment, forfeiture or restoration of property believed to be derived directly or indirectly from criminal activity
issue a look-out circular against an absconding accused
order the demolition of illegal structures used in crime
explanation: Section 107 of the BNSS allows a Magistrate, on the application of an investigating police officer with the approval of the Superintendent or Commissioner of Police, to attach property reasonably believed to be proceeds of crime, after hearing the person concerned. The Magistrate may later order distribution of the proceeds to persons affected by the crime; the CrPC had no comparable power outside special laws.

flags.note: New provision in Section 107 BNSS; confirm the rank of approving officer and the procedure described.
